text:
Hello🙂,

I’m from South Korea, and I’ve been living and working legally in Israel for 4 years on a Specialist Visa (B/1 -  מומחים). On June 8, my partner and I applied for a partnership Visa. My work visa ends on July 12, and we went to Misrad Hapnim today and got an appointment on July 13, they will likely downgrade me to B/2.

Because of the massive backlog in Beer sheva (they are only processing February applications right now) and the fact that I can't work for months on a tourist visa, we think it's best for me to fly back to Korea on July 12 and manage the process from abroad.

We are trying to figure out the smoothest way to transition without causing problems:

(1) The Exit Strategy & The July 13 Appointment: We are torn between two options.

-Option A: Do I fly out exactly on July 12 (when my visa ends) and skip the July 13 appointment completely?

-Option B: Do we go to the July 13 appointment just to ask for a 2–3 week tourist visa (B/2) to pack and say goodbye in peace? Will they refuse to give me a packing visa if we tell them we want to cancel the partnership process and that I'm leaving?

(2) How/when do we cancel the current application? Should we cancel it online before I fly, or does it close automatically when I exit border control? We don't want the cancellation to look suspicious or make them doubt our relationship when we reapply from Korea.

(3) Last day of work vs Overstaying: My employer’s last show/day of work is July 12 (the exact day my visa expires). They are pressuring me to stay and work that day, claiming that flying out a day later won't affect my future visa. Are they wrong? Is it dangerous to be in the country on July 13 without a visa extension yet?

(4) Applying from abroad after 4 years here: Does my clean 4-year history in Israel help speed things up at the while I'm in Korea, or will they treat it like a regular application from abroad (meaning that I've never been or worked here before)?

Thank you for your help 🙏
